title: Lesson 28 - What Agent Script Cannot Express: Execution Model and Failure Modes
description: Explain how an agent works and its basic building blocks of agent script.

questions.question: A prompt instruction tells the model to always run a validation action first, but in production the model sometimes skips it. What is the correct fix?
options: Rewrite the prompt in stronger language
Add a second model call to double-check
Move the run into before_reasoning so it executes unconditionally
Turn off hybrid reasoning for that subagent
questions.explanation: A prompt line is only a suggestion the model may skip, whereas moving the run into before_reasoning makes it code that executes on every parse.

questions.question: An action runs, its gate condition stays true, and the instructions never tell the model to stop, so the model calls it again on every parse. What is this and how do you break it?
options: An action loop, broken by closing the gate deterministically after the action runs or by using a has_run flag
A parse boundary, broken by adding another subagent
A displayable exit, broken by disabling after_reasoning
A guard clause, broken by deleting the action
questions.explanation: This is the action loop, and the platform does not auto-suppress an action, so you give the gate a deterministic closed state after execution or with a has_run flag.

questions.question: Your Agent Script is compiled and run. Which statement describes the artifact the runtime actually executes?
options: The Agent Graph, a serialized execution plan the Atlas Reasoning Engine traverses as a state machine
questions.explanation: The compiler turns Agent Script into the Agent Graph, and the Atlas Reasoning Engine executes that graph as a state machine, not the Canvas blocks or the prompt text.
